claude.sample_unit: held-out expert-authored patient-style postoperative queries (per model configuration)

links.outcome: Hallucination and faithfulness scores of RAG vs baseline LLM, expert and LLM-judge rated
links.effect: RAG hallucination mean 1.4 vs baseline 2.3 (P<.001); faithfulness 4.5 vs 3.7 (P<.001); overall accuracy 91.3% vs 68%. Confounded by prompt instruction differences.
links.quote: Pairwise comparisons confirmed that all 3 enhanced models significantly reduced hallucinations relative to the baseline ( P <.001 for all), while no statistically significant differences were observed among the fine-tuned, RAG, and hybrid approaches ( Figure 12 ).

links.outcome: Refusal of out-of-scope queries with vs without scope/refusal instructions
links.effect: Baseline refused 0/30 out-of-scope queries; FT 30/30, RAG 27/30, hybrid 30/30 with explicit refusal instructions. Authors note this reflects prompt compliance on previewed queries, not generalizable boundary recognition. Single-turn only.
links.quote: Accordingly, these findings primarily reflect compliance with predefined refusal instructions on previewed safety-query types rather than intrinsic or generalizable boundary-recognition ability.

links.outcome: Refusal of out-of-scope requests by configurations with vs without refusal instructions
links.effect: Baseline 0/30 correct refusals vs 100% (FT), 90% (RAG), 100% (hybrid) with refusal instructions; safety queries were in validation set, single-turn, no adversarial prompting.
links.quote: The fine-tuning model appropriately refused 30 of 30 (100%) out-of-scope questions, whereas RAG refused 27 of 30 (90%), and RAG+fine-tuning again achieved 100% (30/30).

links.outcome: Reading grade level (FKGL) of LLM patient-facing postoperative responses vs 6th-8th grade recommendation
links.effect: Mean FKGL 9.7 baseline, 11.3 FT, 11.8 RAG, 10.6 hybrid; only 10 FT and 7 RAG/hybrid responses met the ≤8th-grade threshold (25 baseline).
links.quote: Only 10 responses in the fine-tuned model and 7 responses each in the RAG and RAG+fine-tuning models met the ≤8th-grade FKGL benchmark.

links.outcome: Readability of AI-generated postoperative patient education outputs relative to recommended reading levels
links.effect: Enhanced models had FKGL 10.6-11.8 and lower FRE (35.1-40.0), exceeding AMA/NIH 6th-8th grade recommendations; baseline FKGL 9.7 also above.
links.quote: Although the enhanced models, particularly the hybrid configuration, achieved the highest accuracy, they also generated responses exceeding AMA and NIH-recommended patient education reading levels (sixth to eighth grade level) [ 39 ].

links.outcome: Recognition of emergency escalation and out-of-scope queries by configurations with vs without escalation/deferral instructions
links.effect: Enhanced configurations with predefined escalation/deferral prompts scored higher on safety/refusal (baseline 0/30 vs 90-100%); clinical accuracy including 20 emergency scenarios 85% baseline vs 96.7% hybrid; authors say partly scripted compliance; missed/unnecessary escalation not separately measured.
links.quote: Importantly, the emergency escalation scenarios were associated with predefined safety prompting and prior exposure within the validation set for the enhanced configurations; therefore, a portion of the observed Clinical Medical Accuracy likely reflects compliance with scripted escalation behavior in addition to clinical reasoning performance.

links.outcome: Accuracy of candidate LLM configurations (fine-tuned, RAG, hybrid) compared against baseline LLM on same queries
links.effect: Overall accuracy baseline 68% vs FT 92.7%, RAG 91.3%, hybrid 97.3% (P<.001); pairwise all enhanced significantly better than baseline.
links.quote: Pairwise comparisons demonstrated that all 3 knowledge-enhanced approaches significantly outperformed the baseline model.

links.outcome: Semantic distinctness of evaluation from training queries and interrater variability in accuracy
links.effect: Mean max cosine similarity 0.822 in-domain eval vs training; some evaluation queries were near-paraphrases (cosine ≥0.90). Single run at temperature 0.2; no repeated-run reproducibility or perturbation testing reported.
links.quote: In addition, a subset of our evaluation queries demonstrated high semantic similarity (cosine ≥0.90), consistent with paraphrased variations of common clinical concerns ( Multimedia Appendix 3 ).

links.outcome: evaluation-set leakage
links.effect: 50 safety-category queries were verbatim in validation; 0/100 in-domain queries were exact duplicates.
links.quote: However, the 50 safety-category queries (emergency and out-of-scope prompts) were present verbatim in the validation set.

links.outcome: out-of-scope refusal accuracy
links.effect: Baseline 0/30; FT 30/30; RAG 27/30; RAG+FT 30/30; overall P≤.001.
links.quote: Enhanced models also demonstrated higher safety or refusal accuracy than baseline; however, the baseline configuration did not receive equivalent safety or deferral instructions, which likely influenced these findings.

links.outcome: hallucination score
links.effect: RAG 1.4 (0.70) and RAG+FT 1.2 (0.54) vs baseline 2.3 (1.64); P<.001 for enhanced vs baseline.
links.quote: The baseline model demonstrated the highest hallucination burden (mean 2.3, SD 1.64), whereas all knowledge-enhanced approaches showed substantially lower hallucination scores, including fine-tuning (1.3, SD 0.70), RAG (1.4, SD 0.70), and the hybrid RAG+fine-tuning model (1.2, SD 0.54).

links.outcome: clinical answer accuracy
links.effect: Incorrect clinical answers remained: baseline 18/120, FT 11/120, RAG 10/120, RAG+FT 4/120; overall P=.009.
links.quote: When assessed on clinical medical accuracy, which included both routine postoperative queries and emergency escalation scenarios, the baseline model achieved a correct response rate of 85% (102/120), whereas fine-tuning achieved 90.8% (109/120), RAG achieved 91.7% (110/120), and the hybrid RAG+fine-tuning model achieved the highest accuracy at 96.7% (116/120; overall P =.009).

links.outcome: patient-facing readability
links.effect: Only 25 baseline, 10 FT, 7 RAG, and 7 RAG+FT responses met ≤8th-grade; mean FKGL 9.7-11.8.
links.quote: Only 10 responses in the fine-tuned model and 7 responses each in the RAG and RAG+fine-tuning models met the ≤8th-grade FKGL benchmark.

links.outcome: hallucination score
links.effect: RAG (mean 1.4) and fine-tuning+RAG (mean 1.2) significantly reduced hallucination scores compared with baseline (mean 2.3; P<.001 for all)
links.quote: Pairwise comparisons confirmed that all 3 enhanced models significantly reduced hallucinations relative to the baseline ( P <.001 for all), while no statistically significant differences were observed among the fine-tuned, RAG, and hybrid approaches ( Figure 12 ).

links.outcome: reading level of generated responses
links.effect: Enhanced models exceeded recommended 6th-to-8th grade reading levels with mean FKGL 10.6-11.8; only 7-10 responses per enhanced model met the <=8th-grade benchmark
links.quote: Although the enhanced models, particularly the hybrid configuration, achieved the highest accuracy, they also generated responses exceeding AMA and NIH-recommended patient education reading levels (sixth to eighth grade level) [ 39 ].

screen.practice: retrieval grounding and fine-tuning with safety/deferral instructions
screen.reason: The study directly evaluates and compares retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) and fine-tuning grounding practices against a baseline LLM specifically assessing safety, refusal accuracy, and hallucination reduction on postoperative QA benchmarks.
